summary: @servicetitan/onboarding-ui 18.5.1 ships preinstall Bun-runtime dropper executing obfuscated payload
details: The tarball contains a `preinstall` hook (`node setup.mjs`) that, on `npm install`, downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from GitHub, extracts it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against a sibling `math_init.js` shipped at the tarball root. `math_init.js` is a 727KB single-line, heavily obfuscated JavaScript file (obfuscator.io shape: numeric/string constant array, string-array rotator `WV8StW`, decoder `hc1jfK9` over a shuffled alphabet; sha256 9fc2570b7cef51c1b8df116d144d11ff4096357be7d2c4c6367cfc2509cf1bcc). `setup.mjs` itself contains `_0xNNNN` obfuscator artifacts. Neither `setup.mjs` nor `math_init.js` is referenced by any file under `dist/`, and the declared purpose of the package is a React/MobX UI component library (design-system peers, forms, Pusher, contentful) — a UI library has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime at install time and execute an obfuscated blob under it. Executing the payload under Bun (rather than Node) also evades Node-oriented auditing. The runtime fetch is from an official Bun release URL, but the executed content is the shipped obfuscated blob, not Bun itself — the dropper is the fetch-and-exec of that opaque blob under a freshly-installed alternate runtime, triggered automatically by `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
